title: Sliding Window Median
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of `n` integers and a window size `k`. A window of size `k` starts at the left end of the array and moves one position to the right at a time, until it reaches the right end. This gives `n - k + 1` windows. Report the median of every window, in order.

The **median** of a window is its middle value after sorting. If `k` is odd it is the single middle element. If `k` is even it is the average of the two middle elements.

To keep the output in integers, print **twice the median** for each window: for odd `k` that is `2 * middle`, for even `k` it is the sum of the two middle elements.

**Follow-up:** the numbers may arrive as a data stream. Can you support moving the window forward by one element in `O(log k)` time?
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print `n - k + 1` space-separated integers: twice the median of each window, from left to right.

examples.explanation: Window [2,10,4,6] sorts to 2 4 6 10; the two middle values are 4 and 6, so the sum is 10 (median 5). Window [10,4,6,12] sorts to 4 6 10 12; the middle values are 6 and 10, sum 16 (median 8).
With k = 1 each window is a single element, and the doubled median is just twice that element.

hints: Sorting every window costs O(k log k) per step, far too slow. You only need the middle one or two elements, so keep the window split into a lower half and an upper half.
Use a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, kept balanced so their sizes differ by at most one. The median can then be read off the heap tops.

Heaps cannot delete an arbitrary element cheaply. Use lazy deletion: record the outgoing value in a counter, adjust the logical sizes of the halves, and only pop it when it reaches the top of its heap. An order-statistics structure such as a Fenwick tree over compressed values also works.
